statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). An eighth consecutive hour after the Globex reopen leaves the 28,981.00-29,100.00 band exactly unchanged, with NQ at 29,016.00 (-1.26%) in the lower third of that band, while WTI has slipped from a 103.58 high back to 102.55 and the Nikkei has held roughly half of its recovery off a 62,726.18 low. Range containment alongside genuine retracement in both oil and Japanese equities is the opposite of a no-retracement path, so Tail stays at the bottom of the watch band at 20. Stress rises a point to 77: swap pricing now implies close to a 90% probability that the Fed raises rates on Wednesday, the Korean AI complex is down about 2.5%, and a 4-5% global oil supply outage remains unresolved. Confidence is 87 on two independent NQ quotes, live oil and Asian cash reads, verified reporting and a verified calendar; the VIX at 15.84 and the 10-year at 4.975% remain Friday cash closes rather than live prints.
recommendation: Tail remains at the bottom of the watch band and well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is unchanged at 13:00-16:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the first full cash hour, which is the first US auction to price the weekend AI-pacing story, the Saudi East-West pipeline outage and a near-90% implied probability of a Wednesday rate hike together. Conditional Tail peaks at 24 there, one point below the block band, because the amplifying structure that would justify crossing it has not been observed. The named invalidation for the constructive structural read is a decisive break of the 28,981.00-29,100.00 band followed by continuation on shallow pullbacks; the named confirmation is a further contained European session. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold an unchanged 28,981-29,100 band for an eighth hour at -1.26% as oil retraces from its high and swaps price a near-90% chance of a Wednesday Fed hike
body:
An eighth consecutive hour of live price-path evidence leaves the structural read constructive. NQ is quoted at 29,016.00, down 371.00 points or 1.26% against the reference close, as of 01:15 EDT, and an independent quote on the December contract shows the same -1.26%, so the move is well corroborated. The decisive structural fact is again unchanged: the front-month day range is still exactly 28,981.00 to 29,100.00, the same 119-point band printed in the first hour after the Globex reopen. Eight hours without range expansion, and without a chain of failed retracements, is the opposite of the price path that overwhelms a mean-reversion book. NQ sits at roughly 29% of the band above its low, not pinned at an extreme.

Cross-asset evidence this hour is two-sided. Oil has retraced: WTI is 102.55, up 2.50%, off a 103.58 session high, and Brent is 107.19, up 2.47%, off 108.46. A commodity that produced the original shock giving back part of the move inside the same session is a retracement signal, not an amplifier. The Nikkei closed the gap about half way, trading 63,401.96, down 0.95%, against a 62,726.18 session low. Against that, Korea is the negative outlier: the KOSPI is down roughly 2.5%, and the Asian AI and semiconductor complex has repriced hard, with several Japanese AI-linked names down between 4% and 12%. Hong Kong has been close to flat, opening firmer and slipping back. That combination is a sector de-rating with a wide dispersion, not a uniform index-level liquidation.

The new macro fact this hour is rates. Swap pricing now implies close to a 90% probability that the FOMC raises rates by at least 25 basis points on Wednesday, with the oil shock feeding directly into the inflation channel. That is a material widening of the stress distribution into the middle of the week, and it is the main reason Stress rises a point to 77 despite the oil retracement. It is not, by itself, Tail evidence: the decision is two days beyond the end of this forecast window, and an expected policy move is not a pathological price path.

Two evidence limits are worth stating plainly. The VIX at 15.84 and the 10-year at 4.975% are Friday cash closes, not live prints, so the volatility and rates reads are stale by construction at this hour rather than absent. The shared cross-asset context file carried a partial collection status and a timestamp roughly four hours old, so it was treated as stale and not used; the assessment rests on independently fetched primary quotes and verified reporting. Confidence of 87 reflects that breadth of corroboration rather than an assumption of completeness.

Conditional risk therefore stays concentrated in the 13:00-16:00 UTC stretch around the US cash open, peaking at Tail 24 in the first full cash hour, one point below the block band. The European open at 07:00 UTC is the nearer checkpoint, where conditional Tail rises to 22 as the first deep non-Asian pool to price the story. Beyond the US close, conditional Tail decays below the watch band through the thin post-close and early-Globex hours before rebuilding modestly into Tuesday.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available. Tail climbed steadily through the weekend from 7 at 05:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC, eased to 16, then stepped through 17, 18, 18 and 19 into the Globex reopen, crossing into the watch band at 21 and peaking at 22 in the reopen hour. Since the reopen it has been notably stable: 20, 20, 20, a single 19 at 02:00 UTC and 20 for the last two hours. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first 16 hours, then WATCH and yellow for most of the reopen window with one EA_ON hour. Stress rose without interruption from 61 to 78 and has since settled in a 76-77 band as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated. Confidence sat in the mid-80s through the weekend, dipped to the low 70s while live price-path evidence was unavailable during the Sunday halt, and has rebuilt to 86 as the Globex session produced continuous quotes. Dominant mode was normal for 21 hours, event/whipsaw in the reopen hour, and mixed for the last five.
outlookSummary: Conditional risk stays concentrated in the 13:00-16:00 UTC stretch around the 13:30 UTC US cash open, the first US auction to price the weekend AI-pacing story, the Saudi East-West outage and a near-90% implied probability of a Wednesday rate hike together. The forecast peaks at Tail 24 in the first full cash hour, one point below the block band, rather than entering it on structure that has not been observed. Two nearer checkpoints precede it: the Tokyo cash close near 06:00 UTC, and more importantly the 07:00 UTC European cash open, where conditional Tail rises to 22 as the first deep non-Asian pool to price the story. After the 20:00 UTC US close, conditional Tail decays to 18 through the thin post-close, Globex reopen and early Asian hours, which maps back to EA_ON, before rebuilding to 20 by the end of the window as Tuesday's European session and the Wednesday FOMC come into range. Confidence decays from 87 to 62 across the 24 slots, reflecting distance from observed evidence rather than any expected deterioration in the market.
